title: Striking the Rider Premium Raised for Coverage Not Yet Billed
content:
Memorandum of the premium accounting desk on the rider premium raised where a member has been in force on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders for coverage the plan has not yet billed them for.

## 1. The figure

The rider premium the plan raises for coverage a member has been in force for but has not yet been billed for is the monthly rider premium the rider held carries, multiplied by the coverage months charged, rounded to the nearest cent.

## 2. The coverage months one charge carries

The coverage months one rider premium charge carries are the single coverage month it is booked to.

## 3. The coverage months not yet billed

The coverage months not yet billed are the whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the handling date, the month the rider took effect in counting as one of them.

## 4. The most coverage months one charge may carry

The most coverage months one charge may carry is the whole calendar months from the day benefits became payable to the handling date.

## 5. The coverage months already met out of the medical plan bill

The coverage months already met out of money standing on the medical plan bill are the number of payments posted to the rider premium account.

The money left standing on the medical plan bill is what has been paid on it less the medical plan premium charged on it, and is never less than nothing.

## 6. The coverage months charged

The coverage months charged are the lesser of the coverage months not yet billed and the most one charge may carry, less the coverage months already met, and never fewer than none.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a rider whose monthly rider premium is 16.30 USD, which took effect 5 whole calendar months before the handling date and whose benefits became payable 4 whole calendar months before it, the rider premium account carrying 1 payment.

1. The coverage months not yet billed are the whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the handling date, the month it took effect counting as one of them: 6.
2. The most one charge may carry is the whole calendar months from the day benefits became payable to the handling date: 4.
3. The coverage months already met out of money standing on the medical plan bill are the number of payments posted to the rider premium account: 1.
4. The coverage months charged are the lesser of 6 and 4, that is 4, less the 1 already met: 3.
5. The rider premium raised is 16.30 USD multiplied by 3, that is **48.90 USD**.

Had the months already met come to more than the lesser of the first two figures, the coverage months charged would be none and the premium raised nothing. Every figure above is a hypothetical input.
